content:
maria: customer 'AcmePay' reporting persistent 429s on their Dedicated pool since ~05:20 UTC. They have reserved capacity and were getting steady throughput earlier today.
maria: details from the ticket: client sees 429 + X-RateLimit-Policy: standard even though their tenant is gold-tier. They say requests appear to be hitting a standard pool.
kevin: confirmed from customer logs — header they send: \"X-Redwood-Tier: [\"gold\"]\" (weird array). Getting throttled after ~1.2k rps.
sanjay: oncall, any infra changes around 05:15-05:25? also saw an increase in control-plane errors earlier.
ops-oncall: deploy-bot shows a control-plane rollout at 05:12 UTC: rollout/selector-eval v2.4.3 -> v2.5.0. Could be related.
deploy-bot: Finished rollout "selector-eval" at 05:12:43 UTC (canary->global). No rollback triggered.
alex: hmm — recent change changed selector precedence so explicit header label vs tier label ordering got inverted in policy evaluation. If header is an array vs string it fell back to a different match path.
maria: repro steps from customer: curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' -H 'X-Redwood-Tier: ["gold"]' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate  -> 429 + X-RateLimit-Policy: standard
alex: quick check in control-plane logs (snippet):
```
2026-03-17T05:13:01Z INFO policy-eval tenant=acmepay selector="X-Redwood-Tier:[\"gold\"]" result=matched_pool=standard reason="header-parsing:array->string-mismatch"
```
sanjay: that message matches what I saw. The parser that normalizes header values was tightened in v2.5.0 and the fallback order changed — arrays now drop into legacy-match-route which has lower-priority labels.
kevin: customer is asking for ETA. They lost 6 minutes of throughput spikes and want credits.
maria: immediate mitigation: route them manually to their dedicated gold pool using tenant override, or rollback selector-eval to v2.4.3. Which is faster?
ops-oncall: rollback is fastest for global impact. I'll coordinate rollback and a targeted tag fix after.
alex: for patch: ensure header-normalizer treats single-element arrays as equivalent to string for selector matching, and restore explicit label precedence (customer-tier > generic-priority). I'll open PR with tests.
sanjay: ops-oncall — go ahead with rollback. I'll prep a hotfix branch and smoke tests for header cases.
ops-oncall: rolling back selector-eval to v2.4.3 now (start 05:27 UTC). will post when done.
deploy-bot: Started rollback rolling_update selector-eval -> v2.4.3 at 05:27:12 UTC
ops-oncall: rollback completed at 05:29:08 UTC. monitoring metrics.
maria: pinging AcmePay with apology + credits. keeping them updated.
kevin: customer accepted temporary workaround credits. asking for root cause writeup.
alex: root cause summary I'll draft: selector-eval reorder + header-normalizer treating array as legacy-match caused wrong policy match -> routed to standard pool -> hit standard rate limits -> 429s. Follow-ups: patch, tests, add canary checks for header parsing, add e2e for array headers.
maria: filing postmortem and customer RCA. tagging eng-runtime and infra. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
